questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨1,1,1⟩+t⟨5,2,-4⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨2,-3,5⟩=36.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨1+5t,1+2t,1-4t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1+5t,1+2t,1-4t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨2,-3,5⟩ & =36 \\ ⟨1+5t,1+2t,1-4t⟩\cdot ⟨2,-3,5⟩ & =36 \\ 2(1+5t)-3(1+2t)+5(1-4t) & =36 \\ 2+10t-3-6t+5-20t & =36 \\ -16t & =32 \\ t & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨1+5(-2),1+2(-2),1-4(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-9,-3,9⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(-9,-3,9).$

$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1+4t,-3-2t,4+t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$

The equation has no solution. Therefore, we conclude that the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ do not intersect.

From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(3,1,-4)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨5,2,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨3,1,-4⟩+t⟨5,2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3+5t,1+2t,-4+3t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+5t,1+2t,-4+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-3,2,-1⟩ & =39 \\ ⟨3+5t,1+2t,-4+3t⟩\cdot ⟨-3,2,-1⟩ & =39 \\ (-3)(3+5t)+2(1+2t)-(-4+3t) & =39 \\ -9-15t+2+4t+4-3t & =39 \\ -14t & =42 \\ t & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=-3$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+5(-3),1+2(-3),-4+3(-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-12,-5,-13⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(-12,-5,-13).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+2}{1}=\frac{z-1}{3},\,Π:r\cdot ⟨1,6,2⟩=19.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(1,-2,1)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨2,1,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨1,-2,1⟩+t⟨2,1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1+2t,-2+t,1+3t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1+2t,-2+t,1+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,6,2⟩ & =19 \\ ⟨1+2t,-2+t,1+3t⟩\cdot ⟨1,6,2⟩ & =19 \\ (1+2t)+6(-2+t)+2(1+3t) & =19 \\ 1+2t-12+6t+2+6t & =19 \\ 14t & =28 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨1+2(2),-2+2,1+3(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨5,0,7⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(5,0,7).$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equations

$$
l: \mathbf{r} = \langle 5,3,-4 \rangle + t \langle 4,-2,-3 \rangle, \qquad 	\Pi: \mathbf{r} \cdot \langle -7,5,1 \rangle = -65.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as 

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle 5+4t , 3-2t, -4-3t \rangle.
$$

Now, substituting $\mathbf{r} = \langle 5+4t , 3-2t, -4-3t \rangle$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-7,5,1⟩ & =-65 \\ ⟨5+4t,3-2t,-4-3t⟩\cdot ⟨-7,5,1⟩ & =-65 \\ -7(5+4t)+5(3-2t)+(-4-3t) & =-65 \\ -35-28t+15-10t-4-3t & =-65 \\ -41t & =-41 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point is obtained by substituting $t=1$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨5+4(1),3-2(1),-4-3(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨9,1,-7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(9 , 1, -7).$

$$

To get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=-3$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=3-4(-3)=15 \\ y=-1+2(-3)=-7 \\ z=2+3(-3)=-7\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $P(15,-7,-7).$

Example: 
                    Finding the Intersection Point of a Line and a Plane Given in Other Forms
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equations

$$
l: \mathbf{r} = \langle 1,3,1 \rangle + t \langle 2,1,0 \rangle, \qquad  \Pi:4x-3y+2z-7 = 0.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle 1+2t , 3+t, 1 \rangle .
$$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-3y+2z-7 & =0 \\ 4x-3y+2z & =7 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7 \\ r\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $\mathbf{r} = \langle 1+2t , 3+t, 1 \rangle$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7 \\ ⟨1+2t,3+t,1⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,2⟩ & =7 \\ 4(1+2t)-3(3+t)+2\cdot 1 & =7 \\ 4+8t-9-3t+2 & =7 \\ 5t & =10 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨1+2(2),3+(2),1⟩ \\  & =⟨5,5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(5 , 5, 1).$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Consider the following equations of a line $l$ and a plane $\Pi\mathbin{:}$

$$
l: \mathbf{r} = \langle 2,2,1 \rangle + t \langle 3,0,1 \rangle, \qquad \Pi:\mathbf{r} \cdot \langle 3,-5,1 \rangle = 7.
$$

How can we find the intersection point $P$ of $l$ and $\Pi?$

We start by writing the equation of the line in the form $\mathbf{r} = \langle 2+3t , 2, 1+t \rangle.$ Now, since $P$ must lie on the line $l,$ we can write its coordinates as $P(2+3t , 2, 1+t)$ for some particular value of $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14147783/assets/d3ba164eb98a53c463744e11d6593177ddde2a0a309f752e5d86b30db0d79925.png)

On the other hand, $P$ also lies on the plane $\Pi.$ So, the coordinates $P(2+3t , 2, 1+t)$ must satisfy the equation of the plane as well. Substituting the position vector $\mathbf{r} = \langle 2+3t , 2, 1+t \rangle$ into the equation of the plane and solving for $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨3,-5,1⟩ & =7 \\ ⟨2+3t,2,1+t⟩\cdot ⟨3,-5,1⟩ & =7 \\ 3(2+3t)-5\cdot 2+(1+t) & =7 \\ 6+9t-10+1+t & =7 \\ 10t & =10 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨2+3(1),2,1+(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨5,2,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(5, 2, 2).$
